description: Step 3 of the extern door collapse. Today native code replaces a comparison export with an inline compare because RUNTIME_SYMBOLS grants RuntimeNativeBinding::Comparison(RuntimeComparison::LtII ..) to the validated declaration; a 24-variant enum and a 170-line match un-flatten that back into (BinOp, CmpOperands). The key is a symbol string in a manifest that is being deleted. The by-construction key: the resolved callable identity of the operator itself. World derives once, by the same runtime-prelude resolution body lowering uses, which FunctionId each of <, <=, >, >=, ==, !=, ===, !== resolves to; native codegen, at a direct call whose callee is one of those identities and whose activation operand types form a supported pair (decided with Types predicates), emits Prim::BinOp(op, l, r), which already lowers with typed fast paths and the same widening/strict semantics as fz_op_eq/fz_op_identical. Ordering ops inline only for the five typed pairs Kernel declares, because Kernel has no any/any ordering clause and an unsupported pair must still fault. Deleted: RuntimeNativeBinding, RuntimeComparison, native_binding column, runtime_binding fields on LoweredExtern/ExternDecl, lower_runtime_comparison, lower_typed_cmp, CmpOperands. The fz_op_lt_* exports become ordinary C calls, reached only when a comparison is not statically typed. Proof: fixture matrix on three doors; a native program capture test showing no call edge to Kernel.</2 for typed integer operands; atom<atom still faults identically on interp and native.
title: Inline comparison operators at the call site by resolved callable identity; delete the manifest's comparison binding
